images.title: Fraction to decimal in three steps
images.purpose: Recap the method of turning a fraction into a decimal through an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.
images.composition: Three boxes in a row joined by two right pointing arrows across the middle of the frame, plenty of white space above and below.
exact_structure: Box 1 (teal #0072B2 outline): the fraction 7/20; under the box the note 20 × 5 = 100.
rejection: more or fewer than 3 boxes or 2 arrows
images.takeaway: Find what turns the denominator into 10, 100 or 1000, multiply top and bottom by it, and read off the decimal.
images.description: Three boxes joined by arrows: 7/20, then 35/100 after multiplying top and bottom by 5, then 0.35.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept on writing fractions as decimals.
images.teaching_notes: Students should name the multiplier first, from the note under the first box, before doing any practice question.

image_decisions.why: A three step strip is a quick recap of the method used in the practice.
